question: On a retained scaffold, does revealing fixed enzyme and substrate sidechains to LigandMPNN improve independent joint reference-geometry recovery?
status: Prospective frozen endpoint before new sequence design or predictions; selected scaffold was chosen post hoc from the prior experiment.

reference_scaffold.origin: water_fixed_seed3 RFD3 scaffold from completed 20261002 water-conditioning experiment
reference_scaffold.claim: Imposed hybrid design geometry, not an experimental target structure or proven physically optimal state.

shared_sampling.rf3_seed_handling: Native seed_everything(0) before each input materialization and each single-input engine.run; loaded engine reused. Same seed is not a guarantee of atom-matched noise or bitwise GPU determinism.

intervention.context_hidden: atomize_side_chains=False; protein sidechains hidden from geometric atom context
intervention.context_revealed: atomize_side_chains=True; fixed enzyme AND fixed substrate sidechains exposed as atom context
intervention.interpretation: Tests this complete context intervention; does not isolate Tyr, one interaction or causal activity.

primary.name: Worst chemical-group RMSD after a single enzyme-backbone alignment
primary.atom_reference_semantics: Each [role, residue, atom] identifies the exact sequence-matched enzyme/peptide position; ligand entries identify the unique Zn and water heavy elements. Reference chains are A enzyme, B peptide, C source ZnO component. Actual prediction chain identities are resolved by exact sequences, never assumed.
primary.alignment: Proper rigid Kabsch fit of all187 enzyme C-alpha atoms to the corresponding retained-scaffold C-alpha atoms. No readout atom is included: peptide C-alpha atoms are on chainB, not fitted chainA. No reflections, motif-only refits, best subsets or post-result realignment.
primary.symmetry: For each GLU independently, choose the smaller group RMSD of bijective OE1/OE2 identity or swap while keeping CD fixed. No other atom permutation, histidine tautomer equivalence or peptide register shift.
primary.per_output: For each group, sqrt(mean squared atom displacement) in the common aligned frame, in angstrom. W is the maximum of the eight group RMSDs. Retain all group values and selected Glu permutations.
primary.per_candidate: Median W across all five assigned ES outputs, only when all five are valid. Also retain the median of each group across all five.
primary.paired_comparison: For each sequence seed200-203, revealed minus hidden candidate medianW; group guard uses revealed minus hidden per-group medians within that same seed.
primary.decision: Consistent revealed-context reference-recovery benefit requires all four medianW differences < -1e-6 A AND all eight group-median differences <= +1e-6 A in every pair. Consistent hidden benefit uses all four medianW differences > +1e-6 A AND all group-median differences >= -1e-6 A. Otherwise no consistent joint reference-recovery advantage. Tolerance is numerical, not biochemical or a practical effect-size threshold.
primary.denominator: 8 assigned sequences,40 ES outputs; all40 valid ES and four complete sequence-seed pairs required. Missing/ambiguous identity, group atoms, coordinates or undefined common fit makes the affected assigned output missing; never replace, impute or exclude it. Any incomplete ES assignment yields incomplete_comparison. Forty monomer outputs are essential context with separate explicit missingness; their absence does not alter the40-ES denominator.
primary.unit_of_comparison: Four paired sequence-design seeds. The five RF3 outputs share a trunk and are not independent design experiments or biological replicates.

secondary_context: All187-CA ES and monomer scaffold RMSD, native confidence, and existing metal/base/water/carbonyl/donor distances, approach/donor angles, G7C-M8N distance and all11 amide-register distances. Three-anchor water recovery is secondary and referenced here to the same retained scaffold. Report paired group/contact medians and all samples; no new pass threshold or geometric exclusion.
interpretation_limits: A lower continuous reference-recovery error is not a productive-state, cleavage, activity, barrier or Atlas-efficacy result.

The max-group endpoint prevents a favorable group average from masking the worst group; the no-regression guard prevents worsening group medians from being called an unqualified joint improvement. Groups need not all strictly improve; report unchanged groups or a localized improvement explicitly.

A mixed finite result leaves consistent joint improvement unestablished on this scaffold; it is not equivalence or a universal negative. An incomplete comparison cannot answer the complete assigned comparison.
Imposed scaffold geometry is not independent evidence that its sequence folds or functions. RF3 disagreement can reflect sequence incompatibility or predictor limitations.
strongest_alternative: Re-evaluating RF3 with another predictor or stopping would address model reliability, but would not test the concrete, source-verified omission of fixed sidechain context in the completed sequence-design run. This bounded paired intervention changes one native input setting on the same retained scaffold and avoids another backbone/water search; if it does not improve joint recovery, do not rescue it with new weights, seeds or thresholds.
claim_boundary: Computational joint reference-geometry recovery only, on one post hoc selected scaffold. No catalytic activity, cleavage specificity, physical fold or general design advantage claim.
runtime_limitations: Same pinned official legacy LigandMPNN and RF3 checkpoints as prior run.
Cached MACE descriptors expected absent; preserve actual runtime warning and native missing-feature path in both arms.
One CUDA GPU, two hours andUSD5 maximum; no extra designs, retries or rescue sampling.
